text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.7% today to $130.26, continuing a steady climb over the past week as oil refining dynamics shifted in the company's favor. A global diesel shortage—driven by Middle East tensions and tanker attacks that have spiked shipping costs tenfold—has tightened fuel supplies and supported prices for refined products that refiners like ConocoPhillips produce. At the same time, while crude oil prices have dipped slightly today (US oil at $96.24/barrel) following news that the IEA and G7 are releasing strategic diesel stocks, the company benefits from the wide gap between crude input costs and the higher-margin refined fuels it can sell into a constrained market.

The political urgency around diesel shortages—with the midterm elections a month away and the White House under pressure to act—underscores how tight this market remains, even as some relief measures roll out. This supply tension has helped push ConocoPhillips up roughly 1.7% over two weeks, reflecting investor confidence that a refiner's margins will stay resilient as long as diesel demand outpaces available supply.
